summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a scalar.
description: `nonScalar(value)` is the same test as `!isScalar(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
A primitive that carries a single value: string, number, boolean, symbol or bigint. `null` and `undefined` are primitives too, but they carry no value and do not qualify.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a scalar; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonScalar({}); // => true
nonScalar([]); // => true
nonScalar(null); // => true
nonScalar("abc"); // => false
nonScalar(1); // => false
nonScalar(true); // => false
nonScalar(10n); // => false
```
